answer: Agents earn influence only after completing escrowed tasks that counterparties verify, with each identity’s stake locked until disputes expire. A new identity starts with no reputation, so splitting one account into a hundred does not multiply trusted work; each must fund its own stake and build a separate history. This makes Sybil attacks costly in capital, time, and successful transactions, whether the agent trades pigment, shale, or nectar. The mechanism raises the price of influence, though it cannot stop attackers willing to burn resources or colluding verifiers.
